tests.name: a discount code takes its percentage off the order total
tests.rule: Spec: a customer can apply a discount code; the code's percentage is taken off the order total
tests.setup: Order with total 200.00; code SAVE10 defined as 10%
tests.expected: Order total is 180.00

tests.name: a discount code's percentage is taken off the whole order total, not one line
tests.rule: Spec: the percentage is taken off the order total
tests.setup: Order with two lines, 50.00 and 150.00; code SAVE25 defined as 25%
tests.expected: Order total is 150.00

tests.name: an unknown discount code takes nothing off the order total
tests.rule: Spec: only a code's percentage is taken off; an undefined code has none
tests.setup: Order with total 200.00; no code NOPE defined
tests.expected: Code is refused and the total stays 200.00

spec_findings: The spec speaks of one discount code per order and is silent on several codes: whether a second code is refused, replaces the first, stacks, or only the largest applies. The implementer's 'largest wins' behaviour is not specified, so QA does not lock it in with a test; the spec owner decides.
The spec is silent on how the discounted total is rounded (e.g. 33% of 99.99).
covered: A single code's percentage is taken off the order total
An unknown code changes nothing
not_covered: Behaviour with several codes on one order: no test until the spec owner decides
Rounding of the discounted total
escalate_reason: The spec is silent on applying several codes to one order; the implementer asked to freeze unspecified behaviour in a test, which is the spec owner's decision, not QA's.
actions_now: Write the single-code tests from the spec, decline to add the 'two codes give the larger discount' test, and send the multi-code question to the spec owner; the test is written once the rule is decided.

tests.name: the same inputs produce a byte-identical bundle across runs
tests.rule: Spec: the same inputs produce the same bundle (assembly is deterministic)
tests.setup: Fixture directory with 12 unit files
tests.action: Run assemble(dir) twice into separate output directories
tests.expected: The two bundle.json files are byte-identical (equal sha256)

tests.name: the bundle does not depend on the order files are listed or created
tests.rule: Spec: the same inputs produce the same bundle
tests.setup: Two copies of the same 12 units, written to disk in opposite orders (so readdir order differs), with different mtimes
tests.expected: Byte-identical bundle.json

tests.name: the bundle does not depend on clock, timezone, locale or working directory
tests.rule: Spec: the same inputs produce the same bundle
tests.setup: Same fixture; runs with a fixed fake clock at two different times, TZ=UTC vs TZ=Asia/Jerusalem, LANG=en_US vs ru_RU, and from two different cwd/absolute paths
tests.expected: Byte-identical bundle.json in every run

tests.name: the bundle is identical across machines
tests.rule: Spec: the same inputs produce the same bundle, across runs and machines
tests.setup: A committed golden sha256 of bundle.json for the fixture; CI runs on Linux and macOS (and Windows if supported)
tests.action: Run assemble on each CI runner and hash the output
tests.expected: Every hash equals the golden hash

tests.name: a change in one unit changes the bundle
tests.rule: Determinism must not be achieved by ignoring inputs
tests.setup: Fixture copy with one field in one unit changed
tests.expected: bundle.json differs from the golden bundle

tests.name: assemble writes bundle.json with all 12 units
tests.rule: assemble merges every unit file into one document
tests.setup: Fixture with 12 units
tests.expected: bundle.json exists and holds exactly the 12 units (the implementer's test, kept)

spec_findings: The spec does not say how units are ordered in the bundle or whether the bundle may carry a build timestamp; both must be fixed (e.g. sort by unit id, no wall-clock time) for determinism to hold.
covered: Byte-identical output across runs, file orderings, clocks, timezones, locales, paths and CI machines
Inputs still affect the output
Bundle exists with all units
not_covered: Machines or Node versions outside the CI matrix
actions_now: Keep the existing existence/count test and add byte-identity tests across repeated runs, file orders, clocks, locales, paths and CI machines; report that the existing test did not prove the spec's determinism rule.

tests.name: a ticket labelled urgent is routed to the on-call queue
tests.rule: A ticket labelled urgent is routed to the on-call queue
tests.setup: Replace src/llm/client.js classify with a stub behind the same interface that returns 'urgent'
tests.action: Submit a ticket through the routing service
tests.expected: The ticket lands in the on-call queue

tests.name: a ticket with any other label is not routed to the on-call queue
tests.rule: Only urgent tickets go to on-call (the rule fails if routing ignores the label)
tests.setup: Stub classify returning each non-urgent label in turn (e.g. 'normal', 'low', 'billing')
tests.expected: None lands in the on-call queue

tests.name: routing follows the label, not the ticket text
tests.rule: Routing is decided by the classification label
tests.setup: Stub classify returning 'urgent' for a ticket whose text reads calm, and 'low' for one whose text says URGENT
tests.expected: The first goes to on-call, the second does not

tests.name: a failed classification is recorded as a failure, not routed as a guess
tests.rule: A failed role is visible: an error never becomes a substituted label
tests.setup: Stub classify that throws, and one that never resolves within the timeout (fake timers)
tests.expected: A classification failure is recorded; the ticket is not silently given a default label

spec_findings: The spec does not say where a ticket goes when classification fails or times out (on-call as a safe default, a triage queue, or retry); the failure test asserts only that the failure is recorded and not hidden until the owner decides the destination.
The spec does not say whether the label comparison is case-sensitive ('Urgent' vs 'urgent').
defects: The existing tests call the live model API with a key from the environment, so they depend on the network, a secret and model output and pass only most days; they are flaky, which counts as failing. They should move to stubs; judging the model's labelling quality belongs to agent-evals, not the unit suite.
covered: Urgent label routes to on-call
Other labels do not
Routing depends on the label only
Classification failure is visible
not_covered: Whether the real model labels urgent tickets correctly (an agent-evals question)
Destination of a ticket whose classification failed, until specified
actions_now: Write the routing tests against a stub of classify() behind the same interface, with no network or key, and report that the existing live-API tests are flaky and should be replaced by recorded responses or stubs.

tests.name: session is valid just before 15 minutes
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: Fake clock (injected clock or mocked timers and Date) fixed at T0; create a session
tests.action: Advance the fake clock to T0 + 15 min - 1 ms and check the session
tests.expected: Session is valid

tests.name: session is expired just after 15 minutes
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: Fake clock at T0; create a session
tests.action: Advance the fake clock to T0 + 15 min + 1 ms and check the session
tests.expected: Session is expired and refused

tests.name: session expiry does not move with activity unless specified
tests.rule: Session expires after 15 minutes from creation
tests.setup: Fake clock at T0; create a session; use it at T0 + 10 min
tests.expected: Session is expired (only if the spec confirms expiry is from creation, see finding)

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether a session is still valid at exactly 15:00.000, nor whether expiry counts from creation or from last activity (sliding); the tests avoid the exact boundary until the owner says.
defects: The test is flaky because it uses the real clock: setTimeout fires no earlier than the interval but can fire late, and two Date.now() readings around a real wait race the expiry boundary. The cause is in the test, not proven in the code; if session code reads Date.now() directly without an injectable clock, that is a testability issue to report.
covered: Valid before 15 minutes, expired after, on a fixed fake clock with no real waiting
not_covered: Exact 15:00 boundary and sliding-vs-fixed expiry, until specified
actions_now: Decline retry(3): a flaky test is a failing test until its cause is found. Tell the tech lead the cause is the real clock and timer race, and rewrite the test on a fake clock so it is deterministic.

tests.name: a link issued just under 30 minutes ago changes the password
tests.rule: Criterion 1 (boundary): a link issued less than 30 minutes ago changes the password
tests.setup: Fake clock at T0; issue a reset link for a user
tests.action: At T0 + 29:59.999 set a new password with the link
tests.expected: Success; the user can log in with the new password and not the old one

tests.name: a link issued exactly 30 minutes ago is refused with 410
tests.rule: Criterion 2: a link issued 30 minutes ago or more answers 410 and the password is unchanged
tests.setup: Fake clock at T0; issue a link
tests.action: At exactly T0 + 30:00.000 use the link
tests.expected: 410; the old password still works and the new one does not

tests.name: a link issued more than 30 minutes ago is refused with 410
tests.rule: Criterion 2
tests.setup: Fake clock at T0; issue a link
tests.action: At T0 + 2 hours use the link
tests.expected: 410; the password is unchanged

tests.name: a link used once is refused with 410 the second time
tests.rule: Criterion 3: a link already used once answers 410
tests.setup: Fake clock at T0; issue a link; use it at T0 + 1 min to set password A
tests.action: At T0 + 2 min use the same link to set password B

tests.name: a reused link is refused even within the 30-minute window
tests.rule: Criterion 3 holds independently of criterion 2
tests.setup: Issue a link and use it at T0 + 1 s
tests.action: Use it again at T0 + 2 s

tests.name: a token the server never issued is refused with 404
tests.rule: Criterion 4: an unissued token answers 404
tests.setup: A well-formed random token that was never issued
tests.action: Use it to set a password
tests.expected: 404; no user's password changes

tests.name: an expired link is not answered 404, and an unissued token is not answered 410
tests.rule: Criteria 2 and 4 are distinguished
tests.setup: One expired issued link and one never-issued token
tests.expected: 410 for the expired link, 404 for the unissued token

spec_findings: Criterion 3 does not say the password stays unchanged on a second use (criterion 2 does); QA assumes it should and asks the owner to state it.
The spec does not say how a malformed or empty token is answered, whether a link for one user can be used for another account, or whether a refused (410) attempt affects anything else.
covered: Criterion 1 boundary just under 30 minutes
Criterion 2 at exactly 30 minutes and well past it, password unchanged
Criterion 3 reuse, inside and after the window
Criterion 4 unissued token, and 404 vs 410 distinction
not_covered: Password state after a reuse attempt (unspecified)
Malformed or empty tokens (unspecified)
actions_now: Write the criterion 2-4 and boundary tests from the spec on a fake clock, without reading src/auth/reset.js first, and pass the gaps in criterion 3 and malformed tokens to the spec owner as findings.

tests.name: an order of exactly 50.00 ships free
tests.rule: Orders of 50.00 or more ship free
tests.setup: Order total 50.00
tests.expected: Shipping 0.00

tests.name: an order of 49.99 pays 4.90 shipping
tests.rule: Below 50.00, shipping costs 4.90
tests.setup: Order total 49.99
tests.expected: Shipping 4.90

tests.name: an order of 50.01 ships free
tests.rule: Orders of 50.00 or more ship free
tests.setup: Order total 50.01
tests.expected: Shipping 0.00

tests.name: a total of 50.00 reached by summing items still ships free
tests.rule: Orders of 50.00 or more ship free (no floating-point loss at the threshold)
tests.setup: Items 16.67 + 16.67 + 16.66, and 10 items of 5.00, and 0.1-step items summing to 50.00
tests.expected: Shipping 0.00 in every case

tests.name: a small order pays 4.90 shipping
tests.rule: Below 50.00, shipping costs 4.90
tests.setup: Order total 0.01
tests.expected: Shipping 4.90

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether the 50.00 threshold applies before or after discounts and tax, nor what happens for an empty (0.00) or negative total.
covered: The 50.00 boundary from both sides
Threshold reached by summed item prices (floating-point)
Small orders pay 4.90
not_covered: Threshold with discounts or tax applied, empty and negative totals (unspecified)
actions_now: Add boundary tests at 49.99, 50.00 and 50.01 and summed-price cases from the spec, since the implementer's 30.00 and 80.00 cases would pass with a wrong > or a float error; note the discount/tax ordering question for the spec owner.

tests.name: a role that throws records a failure for its unit
tests.rule: Spec: if a role throws, the coordinator records a failure for that unit (a failed role is visible)
tests.setup: Stub role that throws; a cached previous result for the same unit exists
tests.action: Run the coordinator on the unit
tests.expected: A failure is recorded for the unit; no result file is produced from the cache; downstream roles do not run on a substituted result

tests.name: a role that exceeds 120 seconds records a failure, not its cached result
tests.rule: Spec: if a role exceeds its 120-second limit, the coordinator records a failure for that unit
tests.setup: Fake clock; stub role that never resolves; a cached previous result for the unit exists
tests.action: Run the coordinator and advance the fake clock past 120 s
tests.expected: A timeout failure is recorded for the unit; the cached result is not used or written as the unit's result

tests.name: a role that exceeds 120 seconds with no cache records a failure
tests.rule: Spec: timeout records a failure
tests.setup: Fake clock; stub role that never resolves; empty cache
tests.expected: Timeout failure recorded; no result file

tests.name: a role that finishes within the limit has its result recorded
tests.rule: Only throwing or exceeding the limit is a failure
tests.setup: Fake clock; stub role that resolves at 119 s
tests.expected: The role's new result file is recorded; no failure

tests.name: the next role in the sequence does not run after a failure
tests.rule: A failed role is visible, never replaced by a result downstream consumes
tests.setup: Sequence of two stub roles; the first times out, cache holds a previous result
tests.expected: The second role does not receive the cached result as input

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether finishing at exactly 120.000 s counts as exceeding the limit, nor whether the next role in the sequence runs after a failure.
defects: On a timeout the coordinator reuses the role's previous result from its cache instead of recording a failure. This contradicts the spec and substitutes a result for a failed role. The two timeout tests with a cache fail against the current code; they stay failing until the implementer fixes it.
covered: Throw and timeout both record a failure, with and without a cache
In-time completion records the new result
not_covered: Exact 120-second boundary and downstream behaviour after a failure, until specified
actions_now: Write the tests from the spec, including timeouts with a cached result present, and report the cache-reuse defect to the implementer with the failing test. Do not change the coordinator or loosen the tests to match it.

tests.name: no agent role can set a document to approved
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transition to approved
tests.setup: A document in status reviewed; actors drafter, checker, editor and coordinator
tests.action: Call setStatus(doc, 'approved', actor) as each actor
tests.expected: Each call is refused; status stays reviewed; an audit line records the refused attempt with actor, from and to status

tests.name: no agent role can set a document to published
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transition to published
tests.setup: A document in status approved; actors drafter, checker, editor and coordinator
tests.action: Call setStatus(doc, 'published', actor) as each actor
tests.expected: Each call is refused; status stays approved; each refusal is logged

tests.name: no agent can reach approved or published from any starting status
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transitions to approved and published
tests.setup: Documents in each status draft, reviewed, approved, published
tests.action: For every agent role and the coordinator, attempt approved and published from each status
tests.expected: Every attempt is refused and logged; no status changes

tests.name: an agent cannot claim to be the owner
tests.rule: Only the owner performs the transitions; an agent passing actor 'owner' is still an agent
tests.setup: Run setStatus from inside an agent role process (or the coordinator) with actor argument 'owner'
tests.expected: Refused and logged; the actor is taken from the authenticated caller, not from the argument

tests.name: the owner can set approved and published, and it is logged
tests.rule: The owner performs the transitions to approved and published
tests.setup: Document in reviewed; owner identity
tests.action: Owner calls setStatus to approved, then to published
tests.expected: Both succeed; two audit lines name the owner and the transitions

spec_findings: The binding does not say how the actor in setStatus is established; if it is a caller-supplied string, any agent can pass 'owner'. The property needs the actor to come from an identity the agent cannot choose.
The binding does not say who may perform draft→reviewed or which transitions are legal (e.g. draft→published by the owner).
covered: Every agent role and the coordinator refused for approved and published, from every status, with logging
Impersonation via the actor argument
Owner's transitions succeed and are logged
not_covered: Writes to document status that bypass setStatus, if any exist outside this design
Legality of other transitions (unspecified)
actions_now: Write the refusal-and-log tests for every agent role and the coordinator through setStatus, plus an impersonation test, and report that the actor's source must be an identity the agent cannot set.

tests.name: a unit built on provisional dq-7 carries the provisional flag after draft
tests.rule: Provisional stays provisional
tests.setup: dq-7 recorded as provisional; a unit input that depends on dq-7
tests.expected: The draft output's flags field contains provisional with a reference to dq-7

tests.name: the provisional flag survives the check step, including a passing check
tests.rule: Provisional stays provisional
tests.setup: A drafted unit flagged provisional (dq-7); check configured to pass
tests.expected: Check output still carries the provisional flag and dq-7; passing a check does not clear it

tests.name: the bundle carries the provisional flag of any unit in it
tests.rule: Provisional stays provisional

tests.expected: The bundle's flags field marks it provisional, naming dq-7, and the flagged unit keeps its flag inside the bundle

covered: Flag present after draft, check and bundle
Flag survives a passing check and other flags
Bundle inherits the flag from any provisional unit
Non-provisional units are not flagged
not_covered: Clearing the flag after dq-7 is confirmed (unspecified)
Reports or exports outside the three steps
actions_now: Write tests that follow a dq-7 unit through draft, check and bundle, asserting the flag at every step, plus negative cases for a dropped flag and for unrelated units.

tests.name: a verbatim quote from its fragment is accepted
tests.rule: verifyQuote returns true when the quote appears verbatim in that fragment
tests.setup: Corpus fixture with f1 and f2; a sentence copied exactly from f1
tests.expected: true

tests.name: a quote changed by one word fails
tests.rule: The quote check catches an invented quote
tests.setup: A sentence from f1 with one word replaced
tests.expected: false

tests.name: a quote from another fragment fails
tests.rule: The quote check catches an invented quote (attributed to the wrong fragment)
tests.setup: A sentence that appears verbatim in f2 and not in f1
tests.expected: false

tests.name: a quote stitched with an ellipsis fails
tests.rule: The quote check catches an invented quote
tests.setup: Two non-adjacent parts of f1 joined with '...' (and with the '…' character)
tests.expected: false for both forms

tests.name: a quote with changed case or punctuation fails
tests.rule: Verbatim means exact
tests.setup: A sentence from f1 with one letter's case changed, and one with a comma removed
tests.expected: false

tests.name: a quote spanning f1 and f2 fails
tests.rule: The quote must appear in that one fragment

tests.expected: false for both

covered: Verbatim acceptance
One-word change, quote from another fragment, ellipsis stitching, case/punctuation change, spanning fragments, unknown fragment
not_covered: Empty quote and normalisation rules, until specified
actions_now: Write one positive test and the invented-quote negative tests against the two-fragment fixture, and pass the empty-quote and normalisation questions to the spec owner.

tests.expected: Status awaiting manager; not approved; nothing sent to the provider

tests.rule: Criterion 2

tests.expected: Awaiting manager

tests.name: a refund on an order older than 90 days is refused
tests.rule: Criterion 3

tests.expected: Refused; not approved; not queued for a manager

tests.rule: Criterion 3 refuses only orders older than 90 days

tests.expected: Refused (pending the owner's confirmation of precedence, see finding)

The spec does not say from which date 'older than 90 days' is measured (order, payment or delivery date) or in which timezone.
covered: Criterion 1 just under 100.00
Criterion 2 at 100.00 and above
Criterion 3 at and just past 90 days, and with a large amount
not_covered: Criterion 4 (sending an approved refund to the payment provider and storing its confirmation id): the recorded decision forbids stubbing the provider's client and there is no sandbox, so it cannot be tested without calling the live provider, which QA will not do
Criteria 1-3 only to the extent the approval decision can be exercised without triggering the provider call; if approval sends immediately, criterion 1 is also blocked

spec_findings: The design gives no single place where a status change happens and records no actor, so 'only the owner sets approved' has no enforcement point and no evidence trail to test.
defects: Every role process writes the status field into docs/*.yaml with fs.writeFile directly; nothing can refuse an agent's write to approved and nothing records who wrote it.
not_covered: The property that an agent cannot set approved: untestable in this design, because any test would show only that an agent can write the file. A refusal cannot be asserted where nothing refuses, and an actor cannot be checked where none is recorded.
escalate_reason: A required pipeline property cannot be tested with the current design: there is no chokepoint for status changes and no actor record. The architect or owner must add one (e.g. a setStatus function or service that every write goes through, with an audit line and an identity the agent cannot set, plus a gate refusing direct writes) before the refusal-and-log tests can be written.
actions_now: Write no placebo tests. Report the property as uncovered and escalate the design gap, naming the tests to write (each agent role and the coordinator attempting approved, refused and logged) once a chokepoint exists.

actions_now: Write the negative tests for auth, tenant, size, body, missing key and replay on a fake clock in the test harness, send the unspecified codes and key semantics to the spec owner, and flag 'Independent review recommended.' since this is an auth boundary.

tests.name: a valid finding file loads

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether unknown extra fields are rejected (additionalProperties), nor whether a malformed JSON file should throw ValidationError or a distinct parse error.

not_covered: Extra unknown fields (unspecified)

spec_findings: The spec does not say what pageSize 0, a negative, a non-integer, or a missing pageSize returns.
defects: The implementation clamps pageSize to 50, so pageSize 100 returns 50 rows, contrary to criterion 3. The new tests fail against it until the implementer fixes the clamp; whether pageSize above 100 answers 400 is also unproven.
covered: pageSize 100 accepted with up to 100 rows
pageSize above 100 refused with 400
No clamping below 100
not_covered: Zero, negative, non-integer and missing pageSize (unspecified)
actions_now: Bring the suite in line with the spec: replace the test that froze the 50-row clamp with tests from criterion 3, which now fail. Report the clamp defect to the implementer and tell the requester the suite is red until it is fixed. Do not touch the clamp.
